evidence.claim: Asana publishes OAuth server metadata with authorize and token endpoints and no registration endpoint.
The authorize endpoint is live and sends an unknown client to the Asana login page.
Review is not required to obtain a token. It is only for App Directory publishing.
evidence.quote: Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token.

evidence.claim: Create the app in the developer console at app.asana.com/0/my-apps.
evidence.note: From a search snippet on a third-party site (help.unleash.so). The Make docs say the same.

evidence.claim: Asana aims for an initial response on directory submissions within one week.
evidence.quote: We aim to provide an initial response on app submissions within one week.

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 3600 seconds, and the refresh token can be reused.
evidence.note: From Asana forum search snippets, not read as a page.

evidence.claim: The authorize and token URLs are https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize and https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_token.
Asana OAuth does not support token requests from a browser. The console has a Manage Distribution setting for workspaces. Example scopes include tasks:read.
evidence.quote: Asana OAuth currently does not support making token requests from a browser for security reasons.

evidence.claim: A new access token is obtained by POSTing to the token endpoint with grant_type refresh_token and the refresh token.
evidence.note: From a search snippet of developers.asana.com/docs/oauth. I could not read that page, so this is not confirmed from a page I read.

requirements.detail: You need an Asana account to open the developer console and agree to the Asana API Terms when creating the app.
requirements.label: Asana account

requirements.detail: Add your app's OAuth callback URL under the app's OAuth section. Exact-match and HTTPS rules were not confirmed from the docs.
requirements.label: Authorization code flow with HTTPS callback

requirements.detail: Asana's code samples page says OAuth does not support token requests from a browser for security reasons. Make the token exchange from your backend.
requirements.label: Token requests must come from a server, not a browser

requirements.detail: A forum post reports access tokens expire after 3600 seconds. Store the refresh token and use it to get new access tokens. This is not from the official docs pages I read.
requirements.label: Access token lifetime about 1 hour; refresh token reusable

scopes.note: Asana has an OAuth scopes page. I could not read it, so the full scope list and sensitivity are unconfirmed. The code samples page gives examples of scope names: tasks:read, tasks:write and projects:read.
